637.title: Historical Reconstruction of Mosul under Badr al-Din Lu'lu'
637.author: Historical & Archaeological Survey Records
637.source: Mosul Historical Society & Ibn Shaddad Text Reconstructions
637.description: Historical mapping of medieval Mosul under Atabeg rule, detailing the citadel (Qala'at al-Mawsil), city walls, historic gates, and early Islamic heritage monuments.

912.title: Mosul City Borders & Fortification Walls in 912 AD
912.author: Regional Ottoman Cadastral Records & Historical Reconstructions
912.source: Topkapi Palace Archives & Mosul Historical Surveys
912.description: Mapping of medieval Mosul city boundaries, defensive walls, gates, and major religious heritage complexes.

1096.title: Plan of Mosul Fortress & City Walls
1096.author: Ottoman Military Surveyors & Imperial Engineers
1096.description: Mid-Ottoman era survey showing inner city quarters, defensive parapets, gate positions, and religious heritage landmarks.

1127.title: Survey of Mosul City Walls & Urban Quarters
1127.author: Ottoman Provincial Mapmakers & Municipal Surveyors
1127.description: 18th-century mapping of Mosul's expanding urban core prior to the major 1743 siege of Nadir Shah.

1778.title: Plan von Mosul (Voyage en Arabie et en d'autres pays)
1778.author: Carsten Niebuhr
1778.source: Royal Library of Copenhagen / National Library of France
1778.description: First scientific European survey map of Mosul. Features precise geometric measurements of the city wall circuit, 12 historic city gates, and riverfront topology.

1838.title: Plan von Mossul und Umgebung
1838.author: Helmuth von Moltke (Prussian Military Mission)
1838.source: Prussian Topographical Bureau / Berlin State Library
1838.description: Topographical military map detailing urban density, road networks, surrounding agricultural fields, and strategic height elevations.

1852.title: Vestiges of Assyria (Sheet 3: Plan of Nineveh & Mosul)
1852.author: Commander Felix Jones (Royal Navy / East India Company)
1852.description: Benchmark high-precision survey of Old Mosul. Details individual building blocks, narrow alleyways (Aha'iq), souk corridors, mosques, and churches.

1906.title: Map of Mosul City 1323 AH (Dalil Musul al-Siyahi)
1906.author: Mosul Municipal Council & Ottoman Engineers
1906.description: Late Ottoman administrative map illustrating public squares, government buildings (Sarai), market areas, cemeteries, and historic city walls.

1919.title: Mosul Town & Environs (Mesopotamian Expeditionary Force)
1919.author: Survey of India & Royal Air Force (RAF) Photogrammetry
1919.description: Combined ground and aerial reconnaissance map produced immediately after World War I, detailing initial modern road cuts and pontoon bridge locations.

1944.title: Mosul City Cadastral & Urban Plan
1944.author: Directorate General of Survey, Kingdom of Iraq
1944.description: Official cadastral plan documenting major modern infrastructure interventions, including the construction of Niniveh Street and modern railway connections.

1966.title: CORONA Reconnaissance Satellite Map (DZB004032)
1966.author: US National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) / USGS
1966.description: High-resolution 2-meter satellite imagery capturing Old Mosul prior to major modern urban redevelopments and residential expansions.

1988.title: Mosul Urban Planning Bureau & Declassified HEXAGON Satellite Survey
1988.author: US NRO / Iraqi Ministry of Planning & Municipal Bureau
1988.description: Comprehensive mapping of modern road networks, concrete bridge connections across the Tigris, and urban expansion outside the historical wall line.

2003.title: DigitalGlobe QuickBird-2 Satellite Survey & GIS Footprints
2003.author: DigitalGlobe / Mosul University Urban Planning Dept.
2003.description: Pre-conflict digital GIS vector baseline detailing all building footprints, heritage monuments, and transportation infrastructure in Old Mosul.

2020.title: UNESCO Revive the Spirit of Mosul Urban Heritage Map
2020.author: UNESCO / UN-Habitat / Mosul Heritage Initiative
2020.source: UNESCO Mosul Damage Assessment & Vector Survey
2020.description: Post-conflict damage assessment and vector reconstruction survey, documenting current building blocks, restored landmarks, and modern urban layout.
